properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 7 at 6:34AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description: ...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...  Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus Counties.  .Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon due to  excessive hydrilla growth along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau. The hydrilla has been acting like a dam and holding water back, keeping levels elevated. Water levels are expected to remain steady or gradually rise as rainfall occurs in the basin over the next few days.* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.  * WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.  * WHEN...From this morning until further notice.  * IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river in Citrus and Marion counties.  * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 5:45 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 5:45 AM EDT Wednesday was 28.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 28.2 feet. - Flood stage is 28.2 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3 feet on 10/05/1965. - https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 645 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Death Valley National Park
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 7 at 3:08AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description: * WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110 degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees. This will yield at least major Heat Risk, impacting anyone without adequate cooling and hydration.  * WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.  * WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.  * IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM PDT FRIDAY
